title: The XLS shared-string resolver reads the string table once, and the whole-sheet walk falls from 16,105 reads to 37
code_state: crates/litchi-xls only; no public API, error type, limit or output byte changed; no new unsafe and no new dependency; litchi-cfb needed no accessor
reason_codes: change 0636 attributed 16,055 of the 16,105 positional reads of 54016.xls's whole-sheet walk to one cursor and one read per resolved shared string, and named it for the queue; this removes them
survey item XLS-10's three per-resolve Vec allocations and its linear segment scan are removed in the same change: 5.24 allocations per resolve falling to 2.24 on that walk

the design is all-or-nothing by measurement, not by preference: a temporary trace of every resolve shows the access order has almost no spatial locality, so a sliding 64 KiB window cuts that walk's reads by 65% while multiplying its bytes by 1,057, and reading the table once is better on both axes at the same time
the corpus differential is the oracle: 565 frozen outcomes over 113 fixtures, every one identical, including every typed refusal

open, list and validate are unchanged corpus-wide read for read, byte for byte and observation for observation, and three of change 0627's five range-source selectors carry identical request-sequence digests

a second, independent corpus differential through change 0605's xls_source_attribution agrees: 252 rows, every outcome string identical, all-cells reads -89.54% and full-text -88.83% including the open, no row reading more times

accepted_evidence.counts: a scratch attribution probe over one in-process ReadAt, swept across 126 .xls fixtures (113 open, 565 operation rows) for validate/open/list/all-cells/full-text, both legs, with each row's outcome frozen as a digest
accepted_evidence.allocations: the same probe's counting global allocator over one complete lifecycle, three fixtures x three operations, both legs
accepted_evidence.sst_extents: every fixture's SST record-group extent walked out of its Workbook stream: 108 fixtures with a table, 61 distinct sizes, 8 bytes to 225,003, none above the 256 KiB ceiling
accepted_evidence.range_source: change 0627's five XLS range-source selectors on 54016.xls at its transport (1 ms fixed service, 100 MiB/s, 64 KiB maximum range), three retained samples, both legs, compared on physical request counts, bytes, the complete ordered request-sequence SHA-256 and the frozen observation
accepted_evidence.instructions: callgrind isolation pairs N=2 and N=6 differenced and divided by 4, five scenarios; perf stat -r 5 isolation pairs N=20 and N=120 differenced and divided by 100, six scenarios, cycles beside instructions
accepted_evidence.timing: 120 samples per leg, order A1 B1 B2 A2 on CPU 23, seven scenarios over owned and FileSource sources, with the A/A and B/B floors of the same window beside every paired delta
accepted_evidence.policy_simulation: the resolve traces replayed against six sliding-window ceilings with and without change 0568's growth schedule, a span-sized window, and the implemented whole-table policy
accepted_evidence.attribution_counters: change 0605's xls_source_attribution binary, an independent instrument with its own counters and its own oracle, on 54016.xls in owned-readat and file-source modes for all-cells and full-text (16,145 reads and 16,117 observations become 77 and 49), and swept over the whole corpus, 252 rows per leg, every outcome string identical and no row reading more times

accepted_costs.retained_bytes: one window of at most 256 KiB per resolver, allocated once and released with the scan; measured high-water marks are the fixtures' table sizes, 225,003 bytes at the largest
accepted_costs.over_read_at_the_threshold: a scan that resolves just past eight strings reads the whole table for them; 59858.xls's walk is the corpus's instance and reads 15,630 more bytes for 17 fewer reads, still 18.73% cheaper in cycles
accepted_costs.observation_width: a resolve served from the retained table takes no read and so no observation, which moves the point at which a mutation is reported from the resolve after it to the fill after it, bounded by the operation-level ensure_current bracket that is unchanged
accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and this change adds one bulk copy, which is why perf stat cycles are reported beside it and the two agree
accepted_costs.modelled_range_service: the range-source elapsed figures are sleep-driven model arithmetic over a deterministic request count, not observed service
accepted_costs.measurement_windows: three perf stat windows and three paired-timing windows were run, because two later edits (a defensive sst_region fence, then the review fixes) changed the after binary; all are retained, the instruction column repeats to within 0.53 points and every timing scenario to within 3.3 points at p50, and the third window -- the one whose binaries are named above -- is the one the record quotes

known_gaps.large_tables: a workbook whose string table exceeds 256 KiB gains nothing and is not measured; no fixture in this corpus is in that class
known_gaps.unswept_constants: the 256 KiB ceiling and the eight-resolve threshold are not swept and are not derived from a cost model
known_gaps.open_unchanged: the open still reads and scans the whole string table to build the entry locators; this change is only about what happens afterwards
known_gaps.peak_rss: the window's high-water mark is reported as a bound, not as an observation; no RSS measurement was taken
known_gaps.cold_cache: the FileSource leg runs over a warm page cache and measures pread/fstat call count, not physical I/O
known_gaps.window_allocation_failure: an allocator that cannot hand out the table drops the resolver back to the per-entry path, so the refusal this change introduces cannot make an operation fail that would otherwise succeed; no allocator hook exists in this crate's test binaries to force that branch, so it is argued from the code and not demonstrated

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, concurrency-scaling or cross-platform result
any claim about workbooks whose string table exceeds the ceiling
